proof.observed: ok 18.225s, twenty runs under -race at the new pin, no failure and no data race. My TestStoredOrderBackfillStampOverAnUnstoredEdit and TestAnEditWhoseForkWentAndWhoseRoomHasCommittedIsRefusedAsUnavailable are in the family run above and pass.
proof.negativeControl: Round 5's: the same test red within five runs when the lock is moved back to the first append (`bob's edit is stored in 2 rows, want 1`). The mutation was not repeated at this head; what changed under it is the CRDT, not the lock, and twenty clean race runs is the measurement that pin asks for.

memory.why: The tree's OOM rule, and the first run of mine under it.
memory.how: A bounded sampler of /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.usage_in_bytes every 2 s, started as the harness's own named background job (mem-sampler-infra-707, pid 4486) and stopped with proc://mem-sampler-infra-707/kill at the end of the runs - the form that works in this shell, where $!, jobs -p, kill %1 and $BASHPID all fail.
memory.result: 711 samples over 24m36s covering the family run, the race runs and the soak: sampled peak 2.55 GiB of the container's 19.0 GiB limit, minimum 1.95 GiB. So the docs suite under -p 1 with GOMAXPROCS=4 and GOMEMLIMIT=12GiB uses about an eighth of the limit on this pod, and nothing here approaches the OOM that stopped INFRA-771. The figure is a sampled peak: a spike shorter than 2 s is missed, and the cgroup serves no max_usage_in_bytes under gVisor to check it against.
